findings.text: the trust verdict is recomputed on every 0.5 s loop pass while the checkout stays untrusted, with no interval, deferral or backoff: moved_checkout_is_trustworthy runs a git status subprocess over reckon/ and skills/ each pass (reckon/checkout_trust.py:733), and when the tree is clean but does not import it spawns an interpreter that imports every module and records nothing (reckon/checkout_trust.py:849-868), so a checkout that stays untrusted makes the supervisor spend most of each pass inside a probe and answer its FIFO at the probe's cadence rather than at REQUEST_WAIT_SECONDS; the repository's owner of this decision paces exactly this, gating on FOLLOWER_FRESHNESS_SECONDS and backing off with jitter and a doubling gap for a timed-out probe (reckon/crew/follower_reload.py:333-343, 373-400).

assert calls[0]["adopted"] == {"demo": recorded} compares two readings of recorded_service_pid on the same runtime tree, one taken before the move and one inside the exec_ stand-in, so it would still hold if that reader returned a constant; the arm's independence comes from line 248 (os.kill liveness) and line 249 (the service process's own single start marker), not from this line.

_supervisor_source_root and _checkout_code_is_trusted restate queue_admission.py:672-694 body for body, and _source_code_stamp restates queue_admission.py:660-668, so how a long-running reckon process resolves its checkout root and asks the trusted-checkout question now has two more copies to keep in step with the owner; reckon/served_code.py:813 moved_checkout already exposes the moved-and-trusted decision publicly and was not extended.
